[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (5) The court may at any stage of proceedings make a costs capping order against all or any of the parties, if –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (a) it is in the interests of justice to do so;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (b) there is a substantial risk that without such an order costs will be disproportionately incurred; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (c) it is not satisfied that the risk in subparagraph (b) can be adequately controlled by –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (i) case management directions or orders made under this Part; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (ii) detailed assessment of costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (6) In considering whether to exercise its discretion under this rule, the court will consider all the circumstances of the case, including –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (a) whether there is a substantial imbalance between the financial position of the parties;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (b) whether the costs of determining the amount of the cap are likely to be proportionate to the overall costs of the litigation;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (c) the stage which the proceedings have reached; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (d) the costs which have been incurred to date and the future costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (7) A costs capping order, once made, will limit the costs recoverable by the party subject to the order unless a party successfully applies to vary the order. No such variation will be made unless –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (a) there has been a material and substantial change of circumstances since the date when the order was made; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (b) there is some other compelling reason why a variation should be made. ## Application for a costs capping order

## 3.20

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (1) An application for a costs capping order must be made on notice in accordance with Part 23. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (2) The application notice must –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (a) set out –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (i) whether the costs capping order is in respect of the whole of the litigation or a particular issue which is ordered to be tried separately; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (ii) why a costs capping order should be made; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (b) be accompanied by a budget setting out –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (i) the costs (and disbursements) incurred by the applicant to date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (ii) the costs (and disbursements) which the applicant is likely to incur in the future conduct of the proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (3) The court may give directions for the determination of the application and such directions may –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (a) direct any party to the proceedings –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (i) to file a schedule of costs in the form set out in paragraph 3 of Practice Direction 3E – Costs capping;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (ii) to file written submissions on all or any part of the issues arising;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (b) fix the date and time estimate of the hearing of the application;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (c) indicate whether the judge hearing the application will sit with an assessor at the hearing of the application; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.20] (d) include any further directions as the court sees fit. ## Application to vary a costs capping order

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Application to vary a costs capping order] 3.21 An application to vary a costs capping order must be made by application notice pursuant to Part 23. ## Footnotes
